Abstract
We develop criteria based on a calibration argument via discrete PDE and semidiscrete optimal
transport, for ﬁnding sharp isoperimetric inequalities of the form (♯Ω)d−1 ≤C(♯−→

continuum, and answers a question appearing in Hamamuki [32], extending that work valid for rectangular
grids, to a larger class of graphs, including graphs dual to simplicial meshes of equal volume. We also

the continuum case and in the Zd-graph case is now played by a geometric cell-optimization constant,
where the optimization problem is like in Minkowski’s proof of his classical theorem for convex polyhedra.
Finally, we study the optimal constant in the related discrete Neumann boundary problem, and present a
series of possible directions for a further classiﬁcation of discrete edge-isoperimetric constants and shapes.

Connection between diﬀerent ﬁelds
We focus only two of many possible strategies for (1.3):
(a) A proof strategy of Gromov [28], based on Knothe’s transport plans [37], then improved based on the

In the discrete case the Cabr´e setup was generalized by [32] in the case of orthogonal product lattices,

1.3
Discrete optimum isoperimetric inequalities via PDE and Optimal Trans-

A very large variety of isoperimetric inequalities on graphs are known, valid in varying generality, see e.g.
[9, 6] for edge-isoperimetric inequalities in the grid and in other graphs. See [7] [31][8],[50], [10] [35] as well

The criteria we ﬁnd for the existence of a discrete sharp isoperimetric inequality like (1.3) in geometric
graphs, will include the possibility of adding speciﬁc edge weights. We will see in Section 5 that our results
include and widely extend the ones from [32]. On the other hand, we also see that the form (1.3) is not
always the sharpest form of the inequality that one should expect, as exempliﬁed by the case of the triangular
graph, in which we get (1.16) (see Section 5.4.3 for the proof). This is an interesting new level of complexity
for the discrete isoperimetric problem, compared to the continuum isoperimetric inequality.

Abstract: We develop criteria based on a calibration argument via discrete PDE and semidiscrete optimal transport, for ﬁnding sharp isoperimetric inequalities of the form (♯Ω)d−1 ≤C(♯−→ ∂Ω)d where Ωis a subset of vertices of a graph and −→ ∂Ωis the oriented edge-boundary of Ω, as well as the optimum isoperimetric shapes Ω. The method is a discrete counterpart to Optimal Transport and ABP method proofs valid in the continuum, and answers a question appearing in Hamamuki [32], extending that work valid for rectangular grids, to a larger class of graphs, including graphs dual to simplicial meshes of equal volume. We also connect the problem to the theory Voronoi tessellations and of Aleksandrov solutions from semidiscrete optimal transport. The role of the geometric-arithmetic inequality that was used in previous works in the continuum case and in the Zd-graph case is now played by a geometric cell-optimization constant, where the optimization problem is like in Minkowski’s proof of his classical theorem for convex polyhedra. Finally, we study the optimal constant in the related discrete Neumann boundary problem, and present a series of possible directions for a further classiﬁcation of discrete edge-isoperimetric constants and shapes.
